messages.subject_clean: Estimate on concurrent users supported on basic plan
messages.body_plain:
I would start by reading our documentation <http://docs.rstudio.com/shinyapps.io/Troubleshooting.html#TroubleshootingPerformance> and the Scaling and Performance Tuning <https://www.rstudio.com/products/shinyapps-io-performance-tuning/> guide.

The maximum number of instances <http://docs.rstudio.com/shinyapps.io/applications.html#ApplicationInstances> varies with plan level, each instance would have the memory of the instance type. The basic plan allows up to 3 instances. Keep in mind that when multiple instances are running, each are consuming hours.

There is not a way of routing requests based on the complexity of the task requested.

You may want to create a load test to exercise your application in a representative way, before opening to actual users.

> I'm looking at the basic plan for my shiny app. According to the metrics chart for my app (currently in free plan), one user can use about 180M RAM, about 0.7 worker process.
>
> 1. How do you interpret "0.7 worker process"? Does that mean 1 worker used 70% resource of itself?
> 2. There are some modeling calculations could take minutes even in local machine. In the extreme condition that all users are using the modeling process, I think I need to assign 1 worker for each connection. My calculation is as follows:
>
> instance size: 8G. I think this is the total for basic plan, I can only have one 8G instance (or 8 x 1G instance), right?
> worker memory: near 200M. So 1G instance can have at 3-4 worker, 8G instance can have 24 - 32 worker
>
> That means in the extreme condition the basic plan can have 24 - 32 concurrent users using modeling process.
>
> Is my calculation right?
>
> 3. Some users may also just use the less expensive features, which could take 1 - 5 seconds locally depend on data size. In this case we can have more connections in one worker.
>
> Can I make each worker handle more users for simple operations, and start new worker for expensive operations? The worker load factor seemed to be based on connection count, I'm not sure if this will respond to heavy resource usage.
>
> For example, one worker could take 3 users for simple tasks, and it's serving 2 users now. 1 user start to use the modeling process which take a lot of cpu time, then the 3rd incoming user should trigger a new worker, even the connection count is still within the limit of worker.

This is message is viewable at that URL.

The same shiny app which caused the original problem is also (previously) published at https://amberalpha.shinyapps.io/ppdrelease3 - it deployed fine, and also works fine until a large number is input in the radius widget, at which point the error is thrown which is the title of this thread.  I cannot reproduce this locally, I use only relative filepaths, I have afaik no os-specific or case-insensitive bits.  It is however true that a file gets deleted and written - could I be out of resources?  I have larger apps that run fine, this is not a demanding one.  I have archived three other apps to free up resources - to no avail.  I looked at the js log but does not cast any light (to me - don't know enough to say really).  It is also true that it is 'intermittent' to some degree - putting in a value of 550 sometimes causes the error immediately, sometimes no.

Any assistance much appreciated - I will open a 'basic tier' ticket in 24h if no-one has a solution or a debugging route I can use, but I thought I'd ask the community first just in case.  Apologies for a long post.  Thanks in advance!

Scott,

The graphs are drawn using a javascript library called flot <http://www.flotcharts.org/> which gets it's data from the shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> API in a custom format.

That said, if you're building a shiny dashboard, you might be interested in the showUsage <https://groups.google.com/d/msg/shinyapps-users/rgug4ftiD2c/YvnSIpKTAQAJ> API that is part of the rsconnect package which will return this same data do you as a data frame. You might also be interested in the dygraph package <https://rstudio.github.io/dygraphs/> for plotting time series data in shiny applications.

Hope that helps.
-Andy
